chapters.title: Chapter 274 - Is it really you?
paragraphs: In the Eternal River Sect, chaos had taken over.
Disciples and elders ran in all directions as a column of light broke through the roof of the sect leader's palace, vaporizing tiles and pillars before piercing the clouds above.
No one dared approach. Not even the most powerful elders, who were now flying in the opposite direction.
In the center of this palace, a woman was on her knees, her beautiful blue eyes burning with pain.
She raised a hand to her face, observing the pale disfigured skin for a brief moment before bringing it to her chest, feeling her heart.
"Just a few more years... Is that too much to ask?" She looked up at the black, thunderous sky, her sweet, symphonic voice discordant with her body's current appearance.
She had failed in her goal. She wanted to stay, she wanted to fight more, she wanted to search more. But her time was up.
Being there was against the will of heaven, she knew that, she had always known that.
Even if it was only a part of her soul, that part was something whose existence the primordial laws of that world would never accept.
The fact that she had lasted this long was a miracle.
With a sigh, she closed her eyes, waiting patiently.
Suddenly, a roar woke her up, one she knew all too well.
Her trembling body stood up, her eyes wide as she watched something on the horizon.
Scales as black as night, deep purple eyes and a powerful body that stretched more than forty meters, its large wings tearing through the air at an absurd speed.
The dragon descended with a crash that cracked the ground, its claws opening deep grooves in the stone floor as it advanced towards the throne room.
"Khaedryss..." She whispered.
The light that devoured her body dimmed momentarily as her gaze fell on the couple riding on the beast's back.
One was a man she knew, one of the most talented young men to have set foot in that sect in generations.
But it wasn't this man who caught her eye, not compared to the woman next to him: purple hair cascading down her back, the same color as her gentle eyes now filled with tears.
Elize slid off Qingyi's lap and jumped to the ground, taking a hesitant step towards that figure.
It was strange. That face didn't exist anywhere in her memory. And yet she knew, deep down in her heart, that this woman was someone important to her.
"Little Elize... is that you?" The woman's voice trembled.
She stepped out of the center of the pillar of light for a brief moment. Immediately, the decay of her body accelerated, glowing cracks spreading across her skin.
She raised her trembling hands, trying to reach Elize's face, but her fingers never got there.
"Big sister..." The word finally escaped Elize's throat. Tears streamed down her cheeks as she threw herself into the woman's arms.
"Is it really you? Sniff..." The words came out between sobs.
"Yes, little sister..." The woman ran her hands through Elize's hair, stroking it tenderly. "Look how much you've grown... Mom would be so proud, if only..."
She closed her eyes, remembering painful things.
In a secluded valley, stone roads snaked up to a monumental city, surrounded by walls of reinforced concrete and solid steel.
Tall towers with spiral roofs were guarded by sentries clad in hardened steel armor, only their eyes visible through the slits in their helmets.
In the center, or more precisely, above the city, stood an imposing castle, resting on a floating mountain attached to the ground by colossal chains.
Each link of this chain weighed tons, and each chain was anchored to one of the four corners of the city.
The castle was built of dark gray stone, a fortress capable of sheltering thousands.
The mountain on which it stood had its own forests and valleys, with a massive waterfall plummeting towards the ground, forming a river that cut through the city from side to side.
In one of these forests, a middle-aged man was resting by a stream. Long black hair framed a dignified middle-aged face, with pointed ears and curved red horns emerging from his skull.
His red eyes watched the running water as he wiped his muscular body with a towel.
"Seraphine..." He called out without turning his head, calmly covering himself.

Above him, a large dragon with red scales marked by horrible scars descended. Where there should have been a right eye, there was only a flaming void, the remaining eye focused on a figure approaching from the trail behind.
It was a tall woman, dressed elegantly. A dress the color of her eyes and decorated with black, purple and white roses hugged her curvy body.

A side slit revealed thick thighs and the accentuated curve of her voluptuous, rounded ass, covered by a black bodystocking that also appeared at the wide cleavage of her large, firm breasts, hiding the creamy skin underneath.
They were small compared to boobs like Elize's, but still big enough to more than fill the hands of a man like Qingyi.
Her delicate, rosy shoulders were exposed, thin strips of fabric snaking elegantly down her slender arms and legs.
Deep purple eyes matched her long hair of the same color, while black horns and pointed ears adorned her pale-skinned, porcelain-perfect face.
That woman was Seraphine Vaeldrinn, one of the most beautiful and talented young women in her generation.
The man only gave her a quick glance before turning to the dragon, patting the scales on the creature's snout affectionately.
"What does my dear daughter want with me at this hour?" His voice came out calm and unconcerned, a casual smile occupying his face.
"You know exactly why I'm here, Dad." Seraphine growled low. "Where's Mom? And little Elize? What have you done with them?"
He paused, closed his eyes and considered his next words before answering.
"I did what was necessary." The smile disappeared from his face as he turned to face her directly.
"You know that as well as I do. She is the child of that prophecy. The cursed child. Born with a body different from ours, without a mana heart, without our bloodline. I saved our family."

The dragon descended with a crash that cracked the ground, its claws opening deep grooves in the stone floor as it advanced towards the throne room.
"Khaedryss..." She whispered.
The light that devoured her body dimmed momentarily as her gaze fell on the couple riding on the beast's back.
One was a man she knew, one of the most talented young men to have set foot in that sect in generations.
But it wasn't this man who caught her eye, not compared to the woman next to him: purple hair cascading down her back, the same color as her gentle eyes now filled with tears.
Elize slid off Qingyi's lap and jumped to the ground, taking a hesitant step towards that figure.
It was strange.
That face didn't exist anywhere in her memory.
And yet she knew, deep down in her heart, that this woman was someone important to her.
"Little Elize... is that you?" The woman's voice trembled.
She stepped out of the center of the pillar of light for a brief moment.
Immediately, the decay of her body accelerated, glowing cracks spreading across her skin.
She raised her trembling hands, trying to reach Elize's face, but her fingers never got there.
"Big sister..." The word finally escaped Elize's throat.
Tears streamed down her cheeks as she threw herself into the woman's arms.
"Is it really you?
Sniff..." The words came out between sobs.
"Yes, little sister..." The woman ran her hands through Elize's hair, stroking it tenderly.
"Look how much you've grown...
Mom would be so proud, if only..."
She closed her eyes, remembering painful things.
In a secluded valley, stone roads snaked up to a monumental city, surrounded by walls of reinforced concrete and solid steel.
Tall towers with spiral roofs were guarded by sentries clad in hardened steel armor, only their eyes visible through the slits in their helmets.
In the center, or more precisely, above the city, stood an imposing castle, resting on a floating mountain attached to the ground by colossal chains.
Each link of this chain weighed tons, and each chain was anchored to one of the four corners of the city.
The castle was built of dark gray stone, a fortress capable of sheltering thousands.
The mountain on which it stood had its own forests and valleys, with a massive waterfall plummeting towards the ground, forming a river that cut through the city from side to side.
In one of these forests, a middle-aged man was resting by a stream.
Long black hair framed a dignified middle-aged face, with pointed ears and curved red horns emerging from his skull.
His red eyes watched the running water as he wiped his muscular body with a towel.
"Seraphine..." He called out without turning his head, calmly covering himself.
Above him, a large dragon with red scales marked by horrible scars descended.
Where there should have been a right eye, there was only a flaming void, the remaining eye focused on a figure approaching from the trail behind.
It was a tall woman, dressed elegantly.
A dress the color of her eyes and decorated with black, purple and white roses hugged her curvy body.

A side slit revealed thick thighs and the accentuated curve of her voluptuous, rounded ass, covered by a black bodystocking that also appeared at the wide cleavage of her large, firm breasts, hiding the creamy skin underneath.
They were small compared to boobs like Elize's, but still big enough to more than fill the hands of a man like Qingyi.
Her delicate, rosy shoulders were exposed, thin strips of fabric snaking elegantly down her slender arms and legs.
Deep purple eyes matched her long hair of the same color, while black horns and pointed ears adorned her pale-skinned, porcelain-perfect face.
That woman was Seraphine Vaeldrinn, one of the most beautiful and talented young women in her generation.
The man only gave her a quick glance before turning to the dragon, patting the scales on the creature's snout affectionately.
"What does my dear daughter want with me at this hour?" His voice came out calm and unconcerned, a casual smile occupying his face.
"You know exactly why I'm here, Dad." Seraphine growled low.
"Where's Mom?
And little Elize?
What have you done with them?"
He paused, closed his eyes and considered his next words before answering.
"I did what was necessary." The smile disappeared from his face as he turned to face her directly.
"You know that as well as I do.
She is the child of that prophecy.
The cursed child.
Born with a body different from ours, without a mana heart, without our bloodline.
I saved our family."

chapters.title: Chapter 275 - I promise I'll be waiting...
paragraphs: The moment she heard those words, Seraphine's expression crumbled.
"Child of prophecy? Since when do we listen to those damned old farts? I thought we were better than that!" She roared, her voice echoing through the forest.
"Watch your words, girl." The look on the man's face changed completely.
"I'm the patriarch of this family. I gave you this life and, believe me, I won't hesitate to take it away from you."
The instant his voice ceased, the dragon above opened his jaws full of sharp fangs, roaring at Seraphine.
Its throat began to glow with a threatening orange hue.
But the threat died soon after.
Another roar ripped through the sky in and a colossal creature descended from the clouds, landing behind Seraphine with an impact that made the earth tremble.
If Qingyi had been present, he would have recognized that beast as Khaedryss. But not the Khaedryss he knew.

This one reached over a hundred meters in length, making the huge red dragon seem insignificant, its roar causing tremors to spread for kilometers, trees swaying violently under the pressure of the sound.
She didn't even use mana for it and if she did, all the mortals in the city below would die from the power of her roar alone.
"You claimed Khaedryss? No... that's impossible!" The patriarch of the Vaeldrinn family took a step back, fear finally seeping into his voice.
"No... and I don't need to." Seraphine stepped forward.
Khaedryss opened her jaws. The temperature around her instantly soared, the air distorting as purple and black flames danced in her throat.
The patriarch could only step back and the beast behind him cowered, lowering its head in submission.
Butcher of Empires. Slayer of Immortals.
There was a reason why Khaedryss carried these titles. A reason that the current patriarch of the Vaeldrinn family was too young to know personally.
But from the stories told by his ancestors, he knew enough. And he didn't want to find out any more. Not like this.
Seraphine watched that cowardice, her eyes filling with angry tears as her heart burned.
If she allowed Khaedryss to act, she would declare war on her entire family. And she wasn't afraid of that. Not at all.
She exchanged a glance with the dragoness, who was only waiting for her confirmation to begin the massacre. It didn't matter how many innocents would die in the process.
"Mother would never want so many innocents to die... not just to end his filthy life." Seraphine pressed her face against the black scales of Khaedryss' jaw before turning and leaving.
"After that day, I dedicated my whole life to researching the magic array that Mother had used to send you away, trying to find out how I could go after you..."
Seraphine said as she stroked Elize's long hair.
"In a few weeks of study, I finally figured out how to descend into the mortal heavens."
She paused, an old pain crossing her expression.
"The formation was perfect. We managed to open a portal and Khaedryss went through it. Unfortunately, the heavens of this place didn't accept us.
Khaedryss was almost killed, losing almost all her power. I didn't even make it across, being forced to tear out part of my soul and take this body..."
She closed her eyes briefly.
"I wanted to go after you. I wanted to find you. But I failed. Even after decades, even after..." Seraphine abruptly closed her mouth. "I'm sorry... I failed you and Mother too..."
"It's okay." Elize's words came out between sobs. "We're together now, aren't we? Forever?"
She lifted her face slightly, tears staining her immaculate white dress.
"I'm sorry... but I can't stay. Not yet."
"Of course you can! You can stay with us!" Elize shouted. "You can be my husband's wife too!"
"Your husband's wife?" Seraphine let out a genuine laugh, her cheeks flushing. "Is that how you see your big sister?"
Elize blushed too, realizing too late what she had said.
"It's all right, dear."
Seraphine smiled tenderly.

"What you see here is just a fragment of my soul, disconnected from the main body. I'm not dying. I'm just returning to the immortal sky, taking with me all my memories and everything I've experienced here."
She held Elize's face gently.
"And I promise I'll be waiting for you and yours..." Seraphine gave a muffled laugh. "Husband."
Her gaze turned to Qingyi, admiring his face for a moment.

"Oh, my little sister has developed such good taste in men!" Seraphine let out a high-pitched squeal, her face filled with a happiness she had imagined she would never feel again as she gently pinched Elize's cheeks. "I'm so proud of you!"
After a moment of silence, Seraphine focused her eyes on Elize's.

"Now... can you smile a little for your big sister?" Her voice came out weak, struggling not to cry. "I know it will be a while before you see me. I want to keep your smile with me during the wait..."
Elize lifted her face, wiped away the tears that covered it and then smiled.
A pained, tearful smile. But a smile nonetheless.
"Thank you..." Seraphine returned the smile, placing a single finger on Elize's chest.
A small orb of energy flowed into the purple-haired girl.
In the next instant, the body Seraphine occupied finally gave way, turning to dust in Elize's arms.
The fragment of her soul broke through the sky in a column of violet light.
Elize fell to her knees and was immediately supported by Qingyi. She cried non-stop as the orb of energy left by Seraphine flowed into her mind, awakening memories sealed by her mother.
It wasn't much, she was only six when she was sent to that world. But still, her mother's face was among those memories, clearer than ever.
And that was enough.
"It's all right, darling... just be patient."
Qingyi spoke softly, kissing her forehead and brushing a few disheveled strands away from her face.
"We'll soon reach the immortal heaven. And as soon as we have the necessary power, we'll go after your sister."
"Now, go back to the world of the mind now. Your husband has important things to sort out, okay? I'll be with you soon."
Qingyi's lips descended to Elize's in a soft kiss. When they parted, she disappeared along with Khaedryss.
With a weary sigh, Qingyi found himself alone again.
His eyes focused on the horizon as thirteen figures tore through the sky towards him.

chapters.title: Chapter 276 - Oh, you will be.
paragraphs: "I don't think the seniors are here to congratulate me, right?" Qingyi let out a bitter smile, his hand resting on the handle of the heaven-defying thunder sword.
His eyes swept over the faces of each of the transcendents before settling on Heidu, who shuddered.
In all honesty, he had hardly thought about that fattie after that mission.
He was too busy with his women to waste his attention on some cockroach.
Now he regretted it. Not because it had caused him problems, but because he would probably have to kill people he didn't want to have to kill.
"Don't play innocent, you treacherous brat!" Yanxiao roared, his feline face taken by fury.
"I knew you were with that damned immortal! What else would explain your absurd talent? Hand over your head and tell me where she is now and I promise a quick death!"
He only didn't advance on Qingyi's throat right there because the tigress next to him stopped him.
"My talent has nothing to do with her. And she's no longer in this world." Qingyi replied coolly.
"Besides, I don't think the guardian has the power to decide whether my death will be painless or not. Not anymore. Senile old tiger."
"You..." Yanxiao took a threatening step forward, his Qi exploding in violent waves.
He was about to attack, but the other transcendents restrained him.
"Qingyi." The icy tigress's voice echoed.
"We don't want a confrontation with you. We know you defeated Mochen, we are eternally grateful to you for saving the orthodox way.
But we have received serious accusations about your relationship with a demon, and we want answers about that, this is a crime punishable by death!"
"You did?" Qingyi's gaze slid to Heidu, filled with murderous intent.
The fat man raised his hands defensively "Senior Brother Qingyi, I-I'm sorry, I-I-"
"Oh, you will be."
Qingyi interrupted Heidu with a casual flick of his sword, a line of thunderous Qi emerging from its blade and tearing through the air at an absurd speed.
In the blink of an eye, the fattie's head was ripped off, leaping through the air while staining the fur of Yanxiao next to him with blood.
The eyes of all the transcendents widened.
They had seen the attack perfectly, but they simply couldn't react in time. And that terrified them.

"How insolent!" The leader of the ancestral dragon sect roared. "We know you're hiding that demon woman, Qingyi! We'll turn a blind eye to what's just happened, we'll forgive your crimes, but you must hand her over to us!"
"Not just her," the divine sword sect leader added. "You must also hand over the artifact you use to hide her. We need to make sure you're not hiding anything else!"
"Ah... hahahahaha" Qingyi sighed longingly, before bursting into uncontrollable laughter, his face full of amusement.
"I alone killed Mochen, the one who terrorized all of you like frightened children.
Yet you, or rather what's left of you, think you have the authority to make demands of me?"
Qingyi shook his head, unable to hide his scorn.
Honestly, without even talking about himself, his women would be enough to deal with these bastards.
But he wouldn't use them like that.
He had plenty of confidence in victory. Why lower himself and ask his wives to fight his battles?
"We recognize your power, boy, but you're tired-"
"So are you." Qingyi turned his face to the one who had just spoken, one of the survivors of the four great families.
He had only recovered about 50% of his strength during the trip. But he wasn't worried in the slightest.
He had more than forty million lust points stored up. Even just 50% of his strength was more than enough.
With a sigh, he readied his sword and his lightning Qi enveloped his body in a powerful aura, not inferior to that exuded by the twelve transcendents combined.
There was nothing left to talk about with anyone there.
"Damn..." The leader of the divine sword sect turned to Yanxiao. "What are you waiting for? Activate your sect's defensive arrays! We'll help you maintain them!"
The moment the words fell, Yanxiao acted. His roar echoed through the skies and was answered as the entire sect shook.
The Qi of the sect's main spiritual vein began to drain rapidly towards the walls surrounding the territory.
From the walls, all the Qi began to rise, converging towards the sky in the center of the sect, where the leader's palace stood.
The transcendents quickly surrounded Qingyi, raising their hands and receiving instructions from Yanxiao via sound transmission on how to connect to and control the sect's arrays.
Within moments, Qingyi found himself trapped between the twelve transcendents.
A powerful Qi fell on him like a mountain, immobilizing him in place while more and more energy accumulated directly above his head.
It only took a single moment for him to understand how that defensive array worked.
They planned to use all the Qi of the sect's powerful spiritual vein to crush him in a single blow.
"This is your last chance! Surrender and we promise you a fair trial!"
Qingyi ignored those words, glancing briefly at his status screen.
Perhaps he wouldn't be able to deal with this defensive array in his current state, but in the end, the price for improving his cultivation was only ten million.
One more breakthrough was all he needed to defeat everyone there without lifting a finger.
Closing his eyes, he clicked to improve his cultivation, his body immediately overcome by a wave of strangeness.
There was no pain, just a slight discomfort in his temples, spreading down his back to his feet.
When he opened his eyes again, he saw himself and everyone there in a world without color, just lines and more lines in a universe where everything seemed frozen in time.
Everything but him.
He reached out, trying to touch his own face, but his fingers went straight to his cheeks.
"Ruxue... what is this place?"
"Hmm... See this place as a forge. Your soul is separated from your body and totally connected to the primordial laws.

These lines are the primordial laws, they are everything and they define everything. You have as much time as you need here, but the power of your law will depend only on your own comprehension of the primordial laws."

chapters.title: Chapter 277 - Primordial Chaos Flame
paragraphs: Qingyi sat cross-legged, observing the lines that ran trough his body.
It was... strange.
He still had access to his four primary Qi's, sword, lightning, ice and fire, as well as his bloodline Qi.
But he simply couldn't activate his draconic eyes, or any other bloodline ability.
He closed his eyes. Meditated. pondered. Touched those laws and even used his different types of Qi to manipulate them, observing how they moved around him.
It was only after almost a day in that world that he finally realized what an idiot he had been.
In Ruxue's words, transcendents could try to advance quickly with some useless law, or spend years there to achieve a powerful law.
But he didn't want to spend years there. He wasn't willing to.
Fortunately, he had the system.
If the system store could send powerful techniques straight to his head, why couldn't it do the same with laws?
"System... what's the best type of law I can buy with my current balance?"
[Item: Primordial Chaos Flame Law.
Description: Contains the knowledge needed to master the Primordial Chaos Flame, created by the first chaos god in the ancient era. Requires spiritual roots with two extremely low affinity Qi's.
Grade: No Grade.
"Primordial chaos flame... Qi's of extremely low affinity..." Qingyi's eyes lit up. "That's exactly what I need!"
Without hesitation, he clicked buy.
An intense headache exploded as a myriad of information flooded into his mind.
Qingyi didn't even blink at the pain. On the contrary, he was overcome with ecstasy.
Looking at his own hands, he called out fire in his right and ice in his left, the primordial laws around him shuddering.
His sword Qi and lightning Qi worked so well together because they had a high affinity, flowing perfectly and barely causing fluctuation.
Fire and ice, on the other hand, were complete opposites. The perfect ingredient for chaos.
With a grunt, Qingyi forced those Qi's against each other, forming a ball of fire and a ball of ice, trying to fuse them together.
It should be impossible. They should repel each other, each piece of Qi fighting to eliminate the Qi of opposing power.
But that's not what happened. Qingyi controlled each strand of Qi carefully, tangling them together, a strange order forming in the chaos.
When his palms met, the world around him changed completely.
